source_text: Sed videamus, utrum istud quod definitio praemissa confecit, omnium assensione firmetur. Certe nec prudens hinc ullus potest, nec catholicus dubitare, id est, nec peccatum esse nisi quod potest caveri, nec iustitiam esse nisi quae hoc imputet illi quem potuit, quod libera voluntate per se ipse commisit, cum potuisset cavere.
pass_a_gloss: But let us see whether that which the definition sent ahead accomplished is firmed by the assent of all. Certainly neither can any prudent person from here, nor a catholic, doubt, that is, neither that there is sin except what can be bewaired, nor that there is justice except which imputes this to him who could, what he himself committed through himself by a free will, when he could have bewaired.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Let us see, however, whether what the preceding definition established is confirmed by everyone’s agreement. Certainly no wise person or catholic can doubt this: nothing is sin except what can be avoided, and no justice exists except that which charges a person with what he himself committed by free will, although he could have avoided it.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
